jobs.title: Product Associate / Product Manager, Training & Enablement
jobs.description:
GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2\+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011\. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost\-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026\.



Our culture is candid, analytical, and non\-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit!

**Job Type:** Full\-time


**Location:** This role is fully remote but must be based in Mozambique or DRC only.

**Priority Application Deadline:** October 5, 2026 or until we receive a critical mass of applications


**About this role**



GiveDirectly is planning to grow delivery roughly tenfold by 2028\. Getting there means changing our programs faster and more often than we ever have: consolidating country programs onto a small number of common Salesforce builds through 2027, then layering on new enrollment models — large\-group barazas, remote and self\-enrollment — from 2028\.



Every one of those changes has to land with roughly 650 people in country operations. A new survey design is only as good as the Field Officer's understanding of it at seven in the morning, standing in a village with a tablet and no supervisor nearby. A Country Director needs to know why we changed something and what risk it carries. A Field Manager needs to know what changes about supervision and quality checks. A Field Officer needs to know exactly what to do differently tomorrow, and nothing else.



That translation work is this role. You will turn new survey designs, program changes, and system releases into training materials, live training sessions, demo videos, release notes, and internal communications pitched at the right level for each audience — from Country Director down to Field Officer.



We are looking specifically for someone who has been a Field Officer, or held a directly equivalent frontline role. Not as a nice\-to\-have: this role exists because materials written by people who have never run a registration are consistently too abstract, too long, and wrong about which details actually matter. You should know from experience what makes a training useful and what makes it a waste of a morning.



Your work will be anchored on the 2027 rollout — supporting the consolidation of country programs onto common Salesforce builds, which is high\-volume and has real deadlines — and will absorb 2028 pilot material as those designs become real. Beyond that, you will be a genuinely useful pair of hands to a small, fast\-moving product team: expect a meaningful share of your time to go to ad\-hoc support that doesn't fit neatly in a job description.



We work across English, Portuguese and French. Materials that only exist in English do not reach Mozambique or DRC, and translating them after the fact is slow and lossy. We need someone who can write well in English and work in at least one of Portuguese or French.


**Explicitly not in scope:**


* Designing the programs or surveys themselves — owned by the 2028 Design Lead, the STPM, Large Transfers, and the Senior Director, Product; this role makes those designs usable, and will often be the first person to notice when a design isn't explainable
* Salesforce configuration and technical build work — owned by the Technical Program Managers
* Deciding which change requests get built and when — owned by the STPM, Large Transfers
* Staff development, onboarding, and performance training — owned by the People team; this role covers product and program training only

**Reports to:** Sarah Kenkuyu,Senior Manager Product, LLS


**Level:** Open band — Associate to Manager, depending on the candidate. We would rather find the right person than fill a predetermined level. A candidate with deeper field experience, stronger writing, and the judgment to run their own queue and push back on a poorly explained design will be brought in at the higher end, with correspondingly more independence.


**Day\-to\-day work assignment:** Requests come primarily from the STPM, Large Transfers (2027 build rollout) and the 2028 Design Lead, with the Senior Director, Product arbitrating priorities when they conflict. You are not expected to absorb every request that arrives — part of the job is flagging when the queue is over capacity.


**Travel Requirement:** Regular — roughly once per quarter at minimum, and more during rollout waves, to deliver training in person and to see how materials actually perform in the field.



What you'll do


* **Build the training materials that make new designs usable in the field**
* + e.g., turning new survey designs, program changes, and Salesforce releases into practical training decks, job aids, quick\-reference sheets, and step\-by\-step guides — written for someone who will use them on a tablet in the field, not read them at a desk
* **Write internal communications pitched to the level of the reader**
* + e.g., taking a single change and producing the version each audience actually needs: the why and the risk for a Country Director; the timeline, staffing and cost implications for a Program Director; what changes about supervision and quality checks for a Field Manager or Assistant Field Manager; and exactly what to do differently tomorrow for a Field Officer — deciding what each group does not need to know is as much of the job as deciding what they do
* **Deliver training live, and record it when live doesn't scale**
* + e.g., running training sessions with country teams before a rollout, in person or remotely; recording screen\-capture demo videos of new builds and flows so teams can refresh without waiting for a session; and building a library that new staff can be pointed to r

The RMS Training Lead is responsible for designing, delivering, and continuously improving training programs that support RMS supply‑chain requirements and enterprise‑wide initiatives.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Content Development:** Partner with global supply chain subject matter experts to create e‑learning modules, instructor‑led decks, job aids, standard operating procedures, and simulations; conduct curriculum gap analyses and maintain a version‑controlled master repository.

* **Facilitation \& Instruction:** Deliver in‑person or virtual instructor‑led sessions; provide on‑the‑job coaching, Q\&A, and train‑the‑trainer workshops.

Oversees and manages the operational aspects of ongoing training projects and serves as liaison between project management and planning, project team, and leadership. Assesses training project issues and develops resolutions to meet productivity, quality, and client\-satisfaction goals and objectives. ------------------------


* **Education \& Experience** – Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Human Resources, Education, or a related field *and* at least 5 years of experience designing and delivering training programs for supply‑chain, aerospace \& defense, or government operations.

Today's way of working is drastically changing due to the transition in the working environment, new competitors on the horizon, and advances in technology. Join Lockheed Martin’s digital transformation journey as we accelerate the OneLM Mission\-Driven Transformation through our 1LMX program. The 1LMX ERP Asset Management Team is specifically transforming Lockheed Martin businesses using the latest **SAP S/4HANA ERP** solutions to drive to a common set of streamlined processes and deliver results for our customers. Within this initiative, we are hiring an experienced IT Business Analyst to support our Capital Long Range Planning (CLRP) Team. jobs.title: Escalation Team - Advisor
jobs.description:
**Job Description**

**Job Description**

**The Role:**

The Technical Assistance Center (TAC) exists to support dealers with diagnostic and repair guidance so we can achieve our goal of fixing it right the first time and delivering a positive customer experience. TAC also plays a critical role in ensuring that business intelligence generated through case activity is shared with Engineering and Quality, so product issues are identified, communicated, and addressed.


The TAC Escalation Team (E\-Team) Consultant provides live and remote support to other TAC Consultants and GM dealer personnel to assist with vehicle diagnosis and takes direct ownership of complex or difficult cases. This role determines when to engage a Field Service Engineer (FSE) based on vehicle issues, predefined escalation criteria, and requests from field personnel. In addition, E\-Team members are responsible for identifying, creating, and sharing product issues and resolutions, including service information feedback, preliminary service information, and case\-closing resolutions.


This role partners closely with Brand Quality and Engineering to identify and resolve current and launch\-related product issues. The E\-Team Consultant also supports the organization in building a customer\-centric operating model, developing presentations, and communicating effectively with key partners while maintaining efficiency in a fast\-paced, rapidly changing environment.


**What You'll Do**

* Support TAC Advisors as needed to diagnose and resolve vehicle concerns.
* Partner with Brand Quality and Engineering to identify new and emerging product issues.
* Create and publish bulletins within Service Information.
* Serve as the single TAC point of contact for assigned areas of technical support across:
	+ All GCCX Business Units
	+ Field Personnel including CAMs, RVMs, and FSEs
	+ Executive Leadership
* Exercise sound decision\-making skills to propose solutions to leadership and develop plans that leverage established procedures while creating new solutions when needed.
* Build and maintain strong working relationships internally by exchanging relevant information with colleagues, supervisors, project leaders, and other professionals across the team.
* Create and deliver presentations to support issue identification, resolution, and cross\-functional alignment.

**Your Skills \& Abilities (Required Qualifications)**

* High school diploma with 10\+ years of automotive technician experience, or an equivalent combination of education and automotive technician experience.
* Minimum of 4 current ASE Certifications.
* Customer\-focused mindset with strong interpersonal skills.
* General knowledge of major automotive systems, including electrical, safety systems, restraints, powertrains, transmissions, and chassis components.
* Ability to maintain technical certifications.

**What Gives You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)**

* Master ASE Certification
* Proficiency with GM internal websites and tools including SI, GWM, Salesforce/OneCRM/CXConnect, and Microsoft Office products
* Proficiency with GM internal systems including QIS, PRTS, VIS, Global Connect
* Excellent oral and written communication skills.
* Strong analytical and problem\-solving skills.
* Excellent organizational skills.
* Ability to identify unique situations and escalate appropriately.
* Ability to work independently with minimal guidance.
* Ability and willingness to work in a cross\-functional, team\-focused environment.
* Ability to multitask in a fast\-paced environment and work independently or collaboratively with team members.
